title: Book 6 — Erato, Chapter 101
paragraphs: While they crossed over to Oropos and saved themselves, the Persians sailed on and put in along the coast of Eretrian territory at Temenos, Choereae, and Aegilia. Having seized these places, they at once began to disembark their cavalry and made ready to advance on the enemy. The Eretrians, however, did not intend to march out and meet them in the field; their aim, since the party in favor of staying had prevailed, was to hold out as long as they could by defending the walls. A fierce assault was made on the wall, and for six days there were heavy losses on both sides; on the seventh, Euphorbus son of Alcimachus and Philagrus son of Cyneas, men of note among the citizens, handed the city over to the Persians. Once inside, the Persians plundered and set fire to the temples, in retribution for the temples burned at Sardis, and according to the orders of Darius reduced the inhabitants to slavery.
